subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests, and should that cache live only inside one reviewer/run keyed by the full reviewed input?
rationale: The defect is clear, but caching an exec approval reviewer result changes when a later request bypasses a fresh model review, so the approval-boundary semantics need maintainer intent before automation changes code.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable/session approval.

options.title: Cache only low-risk allows
options.body: Reuse only low-risk allow-once results while continuing to recompute ask, error, and timeout outcomes for a narrower behavior change.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept repeated model cost to preserve one-request-one-review semantics until stronger security or live billing evidence is available.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable/session approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent imported-main history make this the strongest available route for the exec auto-reviewer approval-boundary decision.
